records.issue_text: Six unconditional r.log.Error(...) calls in xorm_store.go fire on every batch including successful ones, flooding error-level logs with ID lists and corrupting alerting
records.rationale: The diff introduces six unconditional `r.log.Error(...)` calls inside the batch loops that will run on every batch even on success, including logging full `ids` lists: two in the MaxAge cleanup (`"Annotations to clean by time"`, `"cleaned annotations by time"`), two in the MaxCount cleanup (`"Annotations to clean by count"`, `"cleaned annotations by count"`), and two in orphan tag cleanup (`"Tags to clean"`, `"cleaned tags"`). These are not gated on `err != nil` and will therefore emit error-level logs during normal operation, plausibly flooding logs and triggering error-based alerting.

records.rationale: The diff does introduce a SQLite-specific branch in `deleteByIDs` that directly interpolates the `ids` slice into the SQL string instead of using placeholders: `sql = fmt.Sprintf(`DELETE FROM %s WHERE id IN (%s)`, table, values)` after building `values` via `fmt.Sprint(ids[0])` / `fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", ...)`. records.issue_text: Restructured test registers t.Cleanup after createTestAnnotations and assertions, so a failure before cleanup registration leaves stale rows with hardcoded colliding IDs (ID: int64(i + 1)), causing misleading cascading UNIQUE-constraint failures in subsequent subtests; cleanup should be registered before creation
records.rationale: In `TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp`, each subtest calls `createTestAnnotations(...)` and does assertions *before* registering `t.Cleanup` (the cleanup is added later inside `t.Run`). If `createTestAnnotations` or the pre-cleanup assertions fail/panic, the cleanup won’t be registered, leaving rows behind in the shared `fakeSQL` DB (initialized once outside the loop). This is made worse by `createTestAnnotations` now hardcoding IDs (`ID: int64(i + 1)`), so stale rows can cause subsequent subtests to hit UNIQUE/PK constraint collisions when reinserting IDs 1..N.
